item.title: Due Week 2b — The Investigator Premise
item.description: For Project 1, write a 4–6 sentence premise. Your priority is envisioning the situation the character(s) are in (or were in).

item.title: In Class Week 6 — Labyrinths and the Traveler
item.description: Playtest groups: Breakfast · Lunch A summary of Project 2’s assignment: A labyrinth is a maze with a story or theme communicated either by how it looks from afar, how it plays from within, or both.

item.title: Due Week 2 — The Exit 8
item.description: Prompt: Play The Exit 8 with classmates. Learning goals: Attention, environmental storytelling, anticipation and surprise.

item.title: In Class — Blade Runner
item.description: Blade Runner is a detective story, a science fiction film that features The Investigator role. Look for the details in the film’s images.

item.title: Project 2 — The Traveler
item.description: Learning Goals: Color theory and lighting; interactive storytelling; arc of experience; game engine literacy; camera principles; materials and textures; sound design; ideation, brainstorming, and prototyping; self-direction; critique.

item.title: In Class — Playtester Questions (Week 4, Day 1)
item.description: Questions for developers to ask their playtesters, when they’re done playing: What happened? Describe a situation when you had a question about your abilities — particularly the actions you can take to discover information.

item.title: In Class — Investigator Milestone Playtest
item.description: After each playtest round, write an answer to these 3 questions on your own private document.

item.title: Due Week 1 — Walkable Artist Gallery
item.description: Using the “Walking Wonders Unity 6” template, create a small art gallery featuring a visual artist’s work.

item.title: Project 4 — Essay Film
item.description: Learning Goals: Self-direction; critique. Team Size: Team Make a pretend YouTube review of your game, as if it is analyzing it after its release.
